zh: 6. 康德的火炉

en: What, ultimately, is the relation between potential and act, faculty and execution, capacity-to-speak and word spoken, the world-context and the facts inscribed within it? In more rigorous terms: what is the relationship
between presence and non-actuality, the not-now and ‘right now’? Or even: between time as a unitary whole and one-or-another position in time?
zh: 归根结底，潜能与实现、官能与实行、言说能力与说出的词、世界—语境与铭写其中的事实之间是什么关系？说得更严格些：在场与非现实性、非现在与“正是现在”之间是什么关系？甚至可以问：作为单一整体的时间与时间中的这个或那个位置之间是什么关系？

en: We know that Aristotle proposed a composite solution: if we are looking at the pure and simple chronological
of an individual being, then we ought to recognise that potential precedes the act; conversely, if we turn our gaze to the temporal

(studying, that is, the genesis and structure of becoming) then we must admit that the act is unconditionally anterior. Both sides of Aristotle’s diagnosis have been put into doubt here: in any case, they must stand or fall together. We have seen that potential is not at all equivalent to a potential act; that the not-now, far from constituting a temporary interlude, is the constant correlate of any actuality. An unrealisable, permanent potential is

posterior to the act from the ontological-temporal perspective; nor, on the other hand, does it appear as its antecedent, or presage it in the chronological sequence. This double rebuttal introduces (or, most likely, presupposes) a comprehensive alternative, which is itself composite and two-branched. If we stick to looking at the calendar, what relation is left between the not-now and the ‘now’ after we have ruled out the idea that the former precedes the latter? And if we instead examine the temporal

(on which the very possibility of the calendar depends), what kind of situation takes shape once we have cast aside the priority of the act (or better, of presence)? To be sure, there is a very close connection between the answers to these two questions. Indeed, the way in which we conceive the potential/act couple
time has decisive consequences for how we conceive its
role.
zh: 我们知道，亚里士多德提出了一个复合答案：如果只考察单个存在者纯粹而简单的年代推进，就应承认潜能先于实现；反过来，如果把目光转向时间秩序——也就是研究生成变化的发生和结构——就必须承认实现无条件在先。亚里士多德诊断的两个方面在这里都受到质疑；无论如何，它们必须同成同败。我们已经看到，潜能绝不等同于潜在实现；非现在远非暂时插曲，而是任何现实性的恒常对应项。从本体论—时间视角看，一种不可实现、恒久的潜能并不后于实现；另一方面，它在年代序列中也不作为实现的先行项出现或预示实现。这一双重反驳引入——更可能说，是预设——了一个同样复合、分为两支的全面替代方案。如果只看日历，在排除前者先于后者的想法之后，非现在与“现在”之间还剩下什么关系？如果反过来考察时间秩序——日历本身的可能性就依赖它——那么在抛开实现、更准确地说抛开在场之优先以后，又会形成何种局面？这两个问题的答案之间无疑存在极其紧密的联系。事实上，我们如何构想时间中的潜能/实现之对，会对我们如何构想它使时间化的作用产生决定性后果。

en: For the purposes of providing a synthesis of the salient point, it seems opportune to turn back – if only for a moment – to Kant’s ‘Analogies of Experience’. After arguing that it is the category of substance that provides us with our only empirical image
time-as-a-whole, Kant focuses on the succession of phenomena

time. He maintains that our experience of the chronological series is hinged on the category of causality. Only the coupling of cause and effect makes it possible to understand ‘the succession of appearances’;

it is only this that allows us to connect a later perception to an earlier one in a non-arbitrary way – indeed, such a connection thus becomes obligatory. The ‘after’ follows the ‘before’ just as a given movement follows its motor. Here, however, arises a difficulty of no little significance: ‘The principle of the causal connection among appearances … applies also to their coexistence, when cause and effect are simultaneous.’
A room is warm
the stove burns: ‘Here there is no serial succession in time between cause and effect. They are simultaneous’.
But how can causality – the intellectual rule that alone allows us to represent succession – play its role when it is itself reduced to a relation between simultaneous elements?
zh: 为了综合说明关键点，适宜暂时回到康德的“经验类比”。康德论证实体范畴为我们提供了作为整体之时间唯一的经验影像以后，转而关注现象在时间中的接续。他主张，我们对年代序列的经验以因果性范畴为枢轴。只有原因与结果的配对，才使理解“现象的接续”成为可能
；只有这种配对允许我们以不任意的方式把较晚知觉连接到较早知觉——事实上，这种连接由此成为必然。“之后”跟随“之前”，正如某个既定运动跟随其推动者。不过，这里出现了一个意义重大的困难：“现象间因果联系的原则……也适用于它们共存的情形，即原因与结果同时存在的时候。”
火炉燃烧时，房间同时温暖：“在这里，原因与结果之间没有时间上的先后接续。二者同时存在。”
可是，因果性——唯一使我们能够表象接续的理智规则——自身被还原成同时存在要素之间的关系时，如何还能发挥作用？

en: What really matters, for our purposes, is the path that Kant takes in order to eliminate this difficulty. We read:
zh: 对于我们的目的，真正重要的是康德用来消除这个困难的道路。原文写道：

en: Now, we must not fail to note that it is the
of time, not the
of time, with which we have to reckon; the relation [of anteriority and posteriority]
remains even if no time has elapsed. The time between the causality of the cause and its immediate effect may be [a]
[quantity], and they may thus be simultaneous; but the relation of the one to the other [preceding and succeeding] will always still remain determinable in time.
zh: 现在，我们绝不能忽视：必须考虑的是时间秩序，而不是时间流逝；即使没有任何时间流逝，［在先与在后的］关系仍然存在。原因的因果作用与其直接结果之间的时间可以是一个趋于消失的量，二者因而可以同时存在；但一方对于另一方的关系——［先行与后继］——仍然始终可以在时间中得到规定。

en: In brief, Kant is saying that the causal law is subject to a double temporal qualification: though these moments appear simultaneously, there is still a scansion of ‘before’ and ‘after’. The two aspects do not cancel each other out, but rather are added together and intersect, because they correspond to two different perspectives: if I limit myself to observing the

of events, I will see cause and effect appearing both at once; but on the contrary, I can see the anteriority of the cause as soon as I take into consideration the more essential field, which Kant calls ‘the
of time’.
zh: 简言之，康德是在说，因果律受双重时间规定支配：这些环节虽然同时出现，其中仍有“之前”和“之后”的分节。两个面向不会相互取消，而是叠加并相交，因为它们对应两种不同视角：如果只观察事件的推进，我会看见原因和结果同时出现；但只要考虑康德所谓“时间秩序”这一更根本的领域，我就能看见原因的在先性。

en: A ‘before’ simultaneous to its ‘after’, the distinction between
and
… the category of causality promises a lot. And, indeed, rather more than it can deliver on. Both the cause and the effect are
actualities, modes of presence; thus both fall
time, and both appear at a specific date. The relation between them, thus being entirely inscribed within the calendar, does not allow for the emergence of any real distinction between the
of time and its empirical

. When we speak of ‘order’ with regard to causality, we mean nothing other than the most extensive and perspicacious examination of the same chronological flux to which the term ‘progression’ refers. The cause, although temporary

to the effect within a circumscribed period, also appears to be its antecedent if we look at a wider period (the stove began burning while the room was still cold). During a certain lapse of time, the preceding and the succeeding coexist and implicate one another: but even so, they remain preceding and succeeding on account of ‘the timerelation of their dynamical connection’.
It is just as true to say that cause precedes effect as to say that cause and effect are simultaneous: but these two statements are true
zh: 一个同其“之后”同时存在的“之前”，秩序与推进之间的区分……因果性范畴许下了许多承诺，事实上多于它能够兑现的承诺。原因和结果都是实现——现实性、在场方式——因而都落在时间中，都在特定日期出现。二者之间的关系完全铭写在日历内部，无法让时间秩序与经验推进之间任何真正的区分显现。当我们针对因果性谈论“秩序”时，所指的不过是对同一个年代流动进行更广泛、更敏锐的考察，而“推进”一词指的也是这个流动。原因虽然在一段有限时期内同结果同时存在，但如果考察更长时期，它也会显得是结果的先行项（火炉开始燃烧时，房间仍然寒冷）。在某一段时间中，先行与后继共同存在并相互蕴含；但即使如此，它们依然依据“其动力联系的时间关系”保持先行和后继。
说原因先于结果，同说原因与结果同时存在一样真实；但这两个陈述在不同的时刻为真。

en: The causal nexus portends something that it cannot sustain. So we must ask whether there is some other conceptual constellation up to the task of fulfilling the promises that causality has neglected to deliver on. Whether there is, in sum, a relationship in which the preceding coexists with the succeeding (without however ceasing to precede it, in a certain period); in which both temporal qualifications (anteriority in the ‘order’ of time, simultaneity in its ‘progression’) are fully valid

. No doubt, such a relationship does exist: namely, that which lies between time as a unitary whole and the single actualities that follow one another within this whole. Total time, permanent and immutable, is the presupposition of any given ‘now’, the undateable premise for any given date, appearing as the ‘already’ or ‘before’ of each given

(whether this be causal or caused). Nonetheless, if we examine the same relation with an eye to chronological progression, we must necessarily reach a different conclusion: precisely because time-as-a-whole is permanent and unchanging, it is always simultaneous to any fragment, or episode, of
becoming; it is on each occasion
to actualities which it also, from a different perspective,
. In the ‘Preface’ to the second edition of the

, Kant catches a glimpse of this paradoxical simultaneity, which is not at all as simple as two events both being present at once: ‘We are unable … in general, to think the stationary in time, the coexistence of which with the variable, produces the conception of change.’
zh: 因果纽带预示了它无法承受的东西。因此，我们必须追问，是否存在另一组足以兑现因果性未能兑现之承诺的概念。简言之，是否存在这样一种关系：先行项同后继项共存，却在某一时期不停止先于后者；两种时间规定——时间“秩序”中的在先性和时间“推进”中的同时性——在同一时刻都完全有效。毫无疑问，这种关系确实存在：它就是作为单一整体的时间同整体内部前后相继的各个现实性之间的关系。总体时间恒久而不可改变，是任何既定“现在”的预设，是任何既定日期没有日期的前提；它作为每项既定实现——无论是作为原因还是作为结果——的“已经”或“之前”出现。然而，如果从年代推进的角度考察同一个关系，就必然得出不同结论：作为整体的时间恰恰因为恒久不变，始终同生成变化的任何片段或插曲同时存在；它每次都与这些现实态同时存在，而从另一个视角看又先于它们。康德在《纯粹理性批判》第二版“序言”中瞥见了这种悖论式同时性；它绝不像两个事件同时在场那么简单：“我们一般无法……思考时间中的静止者；它同变化者的共存产生变化概念。”

en: Even if the permanence of time-as-a-whole is not conceivable ‘as a thing in itself’, according to Kant it can be represented by way of analogy with the invariability of substance. Moreover – still according to Kant – it is possible to portray the succession of phenomena in time thanks to the nexus of cause and effect. As a consequence, sticking to Kant’s lexicon, the relationship between the permanent and the changeable, or between the totality of time and chronological succession, indirectly has to do with the relationship between substance and the causal sequence. Here ‘Now, we must not fail to note that it is [also] the
of time, not [only] the
of time, with which we have to reckon;

and only here do anteriority and simultaneity really go hand-in-hand. We have just seen, however, that total time – which is, of course, permanent, but never fulfilled or realised – is comparable not to substance (whose unalterability is equivalent to an eternal presence) but rather to potential (a perennial not-now). Within finite experience, it is only potential that provides an adequate image of the permanent non-actuality that characterises time as a unitary whole. So that
which appears to belong to the relation between substance and causality ought instead be attributed to the relation between potential and act.
zh: 康德认为，即使作为整体之时间的恒久不能被构想为“自在之物”，仍可通过与实体不变性的类比来表象。此外——仍依照康德——由于原因与结果的纽带，我们能够描绘现象在时间中的接续。因此，如果坚持使用康德的词汇，恒久与变化之间、或者时间总体与年代接续之间的关系，间接关涉实体与因果序列之间的关系。只有在这里，“绝不能忽视：必须［也］考虑时间秩序，而［不只］是时间流逝”；
也只有在这里，在先性与同时性才真正携手同行。不过我们刚刚看到，总体时间固然恒久，却从未得到完成或实现；它可以比拟的不是实体——实体的不变等同于永恒在场——而是潜能——一个永恒的非现在。在有限经验中，只有潜能为作为单一整体之时间所特有的恒久非现实性提供恰当影像。因此，看起来属于实体与因果性关系的东西，反而应归给潜能与实现之间的关系。

en: It thus becomes possible to formulate more explicitly the thesis on which these pages hinge. The potential/act couple, within which the not-now and the ‘now’ confront one another (and not two different ‘nows’, as in the cause/effect binary) is the theatre of both a
and a
. In terms of the temporal
, potential is
to the act: it takes the form of a dateless ‘before’, the mode of existence of an indeterminate past. In terms of chronological

, conversely, potential and act are always simultaneous: potential is not the prefiguration of the act, but its heterogeneous correlate, its incommensurable shadow. Diachrony as well as concomitance each have a special status. Potential and act, capacity-to-speak and word spoken, labour-power and concretely executed labour, world and facts, do indeed represent a ‘before’ and a ‘after’, but a ‘before’ and ‘after’ inserted within one same point of time, bifurcating and splitting it in two. For its part, the chronological simultaneity between potential and act should not be mistaken to mean that both are present at once: after all, one of the simultaneous elements – the potential not-now – is never present. Rather, it means the coexistence of the ‘now’ as such, with its well-defined contents, and a
past, that singular and never actual past which constitutes a faculty’s (and the world-context’s) mode of existence.
zh: 于是，可以更明确地表述这些篇章所围绕的命题。潜能/实现之对——其中相互面对的是非现在与“现在”，而不像原因/结果之对那样是两个不同“现在”——既是一种历时性又是一种并存关系上演的剧场。就时间秩序而言，潜能先于实现：它采取一个没有日期的“之前”之形式，采取一个不确定过去的存在方式。就年代推进而言，潜能与实现反而始终同时存在：潜能不是实现的预示，而是它的异质对应项、不可通约的影子。历时性和并存各自都具有特殊地位。潜能与实现、言说能力与说出的词、劳动力与具体实行的劳动、世界与事实，确实代表“之前”和“之后”；但这是一组被嵌入同一个时间点、使之分岔并一分为二的“之前”和“之后”。另一方面，潜能与实现在年代上的同时性，不应被误解为二者同时在场；毕竟，同时存在的一个要素——潜在的非现在——从不在场。它反而意味着具有明确内容的“现在”本身，同一种独特过去共存；这个奇异而从未成为现实态的过去，构成官能（以及世界—语境）的存在方式。
